Issues in auto_release.sh:

1. In the CI failure output: "Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496" — wait the failure log shows the script said pushed and then errors. Actually the output ordering was: attempt 1, pushed v0.1.496 — hmm, no. Look at the actual failing output again:

```
'Auto-release: v0.1.495 -> v0.1.496 (attempt 1)\n'
'Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496 — the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs fire from it.\n'
'Committer identity unknown\n'
...
'fatal: empty ident name ... not allowed\n'
'error: src refspec refs/tags/v0.1.496 does not match any\n'
'error: failed to push some refs to ...'
' * [new tag]         v0.1.496 -> v0.1.496\n'
```

The stdout/stderr interleaving in the test captured combined output. Actually the order suggests: attempt 1 printed; then the race hook tried to create the racer tag (stderr: Committer identity unknown, fatal...), the racer push failed (error: src refspec does not match any, failed to push); then the script's own push succeeded (* [new tag] v0.1.496 -> v0.1.496); "pushed v0.1.496" printed... The ordering in the merged stream isn't strictly sequential, but the conclusion stands: the racer's annotated tag failed due to missing identity in the racer clone, so the race never happened.

Note the script itself sets `git config user.name "fa-release-bot[bot]"` at the top — in the SEED repo (cwd). So the script's own tag works. The racer clone is the gap. Confirmed root cause.

2. Another issue: `notes=$(bash .../release_notes.sh "$next")` — if release_notes.sh fails, notes="Release $tag". Then `gh release create ... || true` — silently ignores failure. PR description says "one gh release create". The `|| true` means a failed release create leaves a pushed tag with no GitHub Release — the binaries job "can attach assets to it" but there is no release object. Acceptable? It was `|| true` in old code probably too. The test stub asserts one create per run. Not a blocker.

3. `git tag -a "$tag" ... origin/main` — tags origin/main from the fetch at top of the loop iteration. OK.

4. The coalesce check runs before the loop, using `git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag"` — the tag's committer date. For annotated tags, `git log -1` on a tag... `git log -1 --format=%ct <tag>` gives the commit date of the tagged commit, not the tag creation date! For annotated tags, to get tagger date you'd use `git log -1 --format=%ct` on the tag object — actually `git log` dereferences the annotated tag to the commit, so %ct is the commit's committer date. Hmm — with `git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag"`, git shows the commit the tag points to, so the date is the commit date of origin/main's tip at tag time — which equals the tag time approximately since the tag is placed on origin/main's tip. Since the bot tags origin/main's HEAD at release time, the committer date of that commit is when it landed on main — close to release time, but could be older if commits sat pending. E.g., commits merged, then the 2h cron fires 5h later: the tag's commit date is the merge time; tag created at cron time. tag_age computed from commit date could be >2h even at tag creation... Actually wait, that makes tag_age LARGER (older), so coalesce is less likely to trigger — releases more frequent, not less. Conversely, if the commit was just merged, commit date is fresh, tag_age small → coalesce. It's approximately fine but semantically it measures commit age, not tag age. With tagAgeHours test using backdated GIT_COMMITTER_DATE on the seed commit... In the fixture, the seed commit and tag are both backdated by tagAgeHours, so `git log -1 --format=%ct v0.1.495` gives the backdated commit date. So the coalesce test passes either way. Minor semantic issue: should use `git log -1 --format=%ct` with tag object date — `%ct` on annotated tag... Actually for annotated tags, `git log -1 --format=%ct tag` still shows the commit. To get the tagger date: `git for-each-ref refs/tags/vX --format='%(taggerdate:unix)'` or `git log -1 --format=%ct` won't work. It's a minor thing; arguably commit age ≈ tag age in this flow. SUGGESTION at most.

5. The dry-run path: computes and deletes the local tag, exits 0. Good.

6. `grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'` — head -1. Fine.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1522: stamp the staged publish tree with the release version — the git
# tag is the single source of truth, the repo files carry a placeholder
# (0.0.0-dev) and are NEVER mutated by a release.
#
# Usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>
#   <stage-dir> — the staged package tree (scripts/stage_publish_package.sh)
#   <version>   — the release version WITHOUT the leading v (1.0.550)
#
# What it stamps, in order:
#   1. pubspec.yaml `version:` in the stage — and a hard guard that the
#      staged version now EQUALS <version> (a tag/file desync fails here,
#      BEFORE the upload, never mid-publish);
#   2. CHANGELOG.md in the stage — the tag's section is generated and
#      PREPENDED (the repo file keeps its curated `## Unreleased` window;
#      pub.dev's 262144-byte cap is enforced on the STAGED file, which is
#      trimmed of its oldest sections if needed — the repo file stays
#      lossless in git, the archive tail lives in CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md).
set -euo pipefail

stage="${1:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
version="${2:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

pubspec="$stage/pubspec.yaml"
changelog="$stage/CHANGELOG.md"
[ -f "$pubspec" ] || { echo "::error::staged pubspec missing: $pubspec"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$changelog" ] || { echo "::error::staged CHANGELOG missing: $changelog"; exit 1; }

# ── 1. Stamp the version ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $version/" "$pubspec"

# Guard (gh-1522 AC: staged version MUST equal the tag name, v1.0.550 →
# 1.0.550) — the stamp above makes this self-evident, but the check is the
# invariant's tripwire: a future staging change that drops the pubspec
# version line, comments it, or carries a second version field fails LOUDLY
# here instead of shipping a 0.0.0-dev package to pub.dev.
stamped=$(grep '^version:' "$pubspec" | awk '{print $2}')
if [ "$stamped" != "$version" ]; then
  echo "::error::staged pubspec version '$stamped' != release tag version '$version' — refusing to publish (gh-1522 tag↔file invariant)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "staged pubspec stamped to $version"

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):
#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;
#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`
#      (the release "moves Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE
#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
#
# One python step does the whole staged edit: prepend the generated section
# under the file's `# Changelog` preamble (file order is newest-first — the
# stamp prepends), drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became
# the tag's section or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the
# published artifact never shows an Unreleased section), and keep only what
# fits under pub.dev's cap, newest first — the fresh tag section always
# survives. The trimmed tail is not lost: the repo file (git) and
# CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md carry the full history.
section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1
fi
FA_SECTION="$section" FA_VERSION="$version" FA_CHANGELOG="$changelog" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

cap = 262144
path = os.environ["FA_CHANGELOG"]
version = os.environ["FA_VERSION"]
section = os.environ["FA_SECTION"].strip("\n")

text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
parts = re.split(r"(?=^## )", text, flags=re.M)
preamble = parts[0]
versions = [
    s
    for s in parts[1:]
    if s.startswith("## ")
    and not re.match(r"^## Unreleased[ \t]*$", s.split("\n", 1)[0])
]
new = f"## {version}\n{section}\n"
size = len((preamble + new).encode("utf-8"))
kept = []
for s in versions:  # file order: newest first (the stamp prepends)
    b = len(s.encode("utf-8"))
    if kept and size + b >= cap:
        break
    kept.append(s)
    size += b
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(preamble + new + "".join(kept))
PY

# gh-1452: pub.dev server-rejects an upload whose CHANGELOG.md exceeds its
# hard 262144-byte content cap — the guard above already trims to fit, so a
# failure here means even the preamble + the single fresh section is over
# (pathological); a second pass keeping ONLY the fresh section is the last
# resort before the loud fail.
bash "$repo_root/scripts/check_changelog_size.sh" "$changelog" || {
  echo "staged CHANGELOG still over the pub.dev cap — keeping only the fresh section"
  FA_CHANGELOG="$changelog" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

path = os.environ["FA_CHANGELOG"]
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
parts = re.split(r"(?=^## )", text, flags=re.M)
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(parts[0] + parts[1])
PY
  bash "$repo_root/scripts/check_changelog_size.sh" "$changelog"
}
echo "staged CHANGELOG stamped with the v$version section"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring; gh-1522 rework):
#   - scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh — on the STAGED CHANGELOG right after
#     the tag's section is prepended (pre-upload; over-cap trims the oldest
#     staged sections and re-checks);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — on the repo CHANGELOG.md
#     BEFORE staging/upload (the server reject is the worst possible
#     discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

'error: failed to push some refs to ...'
' * [new tag]         v0.1.496 -> v0.1.496\n'

The stdout/stderr interleaving in the test captured combined output. Actually the order suggests: attempt 1 printed; then the race hook tried to create the racer tag (stderr: Committer identity unknown, fatal...), the racer push failed (error: src refspec does not match any, failed to push); then the script's own push succeeded (* [new tag] v0.1.496 -> v0.1.496); "pushed v0.1.496" printed... The ordering in the merged stream isn't strictly sequential, but the conclusion stands: the racer's annotated tag failed due to missing identity in the racer clone, so the race never happened.

Note the script itself sets `git config user.name "fa-release-bot[bot]"` at the top — in the SEED repo (cwd). So the script's own tag works. The racer clone is the gap. Confirmed root cause.

2. Another issue: `notes=$(bash .../release_notes.sh "$next")` — if release_notes.sh fails, notes="Release $tag". Then `gh release create ... || true` — silently ignores failure. PR description says "one gh release create". The `|| true` means a failed release create leaves a pushed tag with no GitHub Release — the binaries job "can attach assets to it" but there is no release object. Acceptable? It was `|| true` in old code probably too. The test stub asserts one create per run. Not a blocker.

3. `git tag -a "$tag" ... origin/main` — tags origin/main from the fetch at top of the loop iteration. OK.

4. The coalesce check runs before the loop, using `git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag"` — the tag's committer date. For annotated tags, `git log -1` on a tag... `git log -1 --format=%ct <tag>` gives the commit date of the tagged commit, not the tag creation date! For annotated tags, to get tagger date you'd use `git log -1 --format=%ct` on the tag object — actually `git log` dereferences the annotated tag to the commit, so %ct is the commit's committer date. Hmm — with `git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag"`, git shows the commit the tag points to, so the date is the commit date of origin/main's tip at tag time — which equals the tag time approximately since the tag is placed on origin/main's tip. Since the bot tags origin/main's HEAD at release time, the committer date of that commit is when it landed on main — close to release time, but could be older if commits sat pending. E.g., commits merged, then the 2h cron fires 5h later: the tag's commit date is the merge time; tag created at cron time. tag_age computed from commit date could be >2h even at tag creation... Actually wait, that makes tag_age LARGER (older), so coalesce is less likely to trigger — releases more frequent, not less. Conversely, if the commit was just merged, commit date is fresh, tag_age small → coalesce. It's approximately fine but semantically it measures commit age, not tag age. With tagAgeHours test using backdated GIT_COMMITTER_DATE on the seed commit... In the fixture, the seed commit and tag are both backdated by tagAgeHours, so `git log -1 --format=%ct v0.1.495` gives the backdated commit date. So the coalesce test passes either way. To get the tagger date: `git for-each-ref refs/tags/vX --format='%(taggerdate:unix)'` or `git log -1 --format=%ct` won't work. It's a minor thing; arguably commit age ≈ tag age in this flow. SUGGESTION at most.

5. The dry-run path: computes and deletes the local tag, exits 0. Good.

6. `grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'` — head -1. Fine.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1522: stamp the staged publish tree with the release version — the git
# tag is the single source of truth, the repo files carry a placeholder
# (0.0.0-dev) and are NEVER mutated by a release.
#
# Usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>
#   <stage-dir> — the staged package tree (scripts/stage_publish_package.sh)
#   <version>   — the release version WITHOUT the leading v (1.0.550)
#
# What it stamps, in order:
#   1. pubspec.yaml `version:` in the stage — and a hard guard that the
#      staged version now EQUALS <version> (a tag/file desync fails here,
#      BEFORE the upload, never mid-publish);
#   2. CHANGELOG.md in the stage — the tag's section is generated and
#      PREPENDED (the repo file keeps its curated `## Unreleased` window;
#      pub.dev's 262144-byte cap is enforced on the STAGED file, which is
#      trimmed of its oldest sections if needed — the repo file stays
#      lossless in git, the archive tail lives in CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md).
set -euo pipefail

stage="${1:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
version="${2:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

pubspec="$stage/pubspec.yaml"
changelog="$stage/CHANGELOG.md"
[ -f "$pubspec" ] || { echo "::error::staged pubspec missing: $pubspec"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$changelog" ] || { echo "::error::staged CHANGELOG missing: $changelog"; exit 1; }

# ── 1. Stamp the version ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $version/" "$pubspec"

# Guard (gh-1522 AC: staged version MUST equal the tag name, v1.0.550 →
# 1.0.550) — the stamp above makes this self-evident, but the check is the
# invariant's tripwire: a future staging change that drops the pubspec
# version line, comments it, or carries a second version field fails LOUDLY
# here instead of shipping a 0.0.0-dev package to pub.dev.
stamped=$(grep '^version:' "$pubspec" | awk '{print $2}')
if [ "$stamped" != "$version" ]; then
  echo "::error::staged pubspec version '$stamped' != release tag version '$version' — refusing to publish (gh-1522 tag↔file invariant)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "staged pubspec stamped to $version"

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):
#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;
#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`
#      (the release "moves Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE
#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
#
# One python step does the whole staged edit: prepend the generated section
# under the file's `# Changelog` preamble (file order is newest-first — the
# stamp prepends), drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became
# the tag's section or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the
# published artifact never shows an Unreleased section), and keep only what
# fits under pub.dev's cap, newest first — the fresh tag section always
# survives. The trimmed tail is not lost: the repo file (git) and
# CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md carry the full history.
section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1
fi
FA_SECTION="$section" FA_VERSION="$version" FA_CHANGELOG="$changelog" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

cap = 262144
path = os.environ["FA_CHANGELOG"]
version = os.environ["FA_VERSION"]
section = os.environ["FA_SECTION"].strip("\n")

text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
parts = re.split(r"(?=^## )", text, flags=re.M)
preamble = parts[0]
versions = [
    s
    for s in parts[1:]
    if s.startswith("## ")
    and not re.match(r"^## Unreleased[ \t]*$", s.split("\n", 1)[0])
]
new = f"## {version}\n{section}\n"
size = len((preamble + new).encode("utf-8"))
kept = []
for s in versions:  # file order: newest first (the stamp prepends)
    b = len(s.encode("utf-8"))
    if kept and size + b >= cap:
        break
    kept.append(s)
    size += b
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(preamble + new + "".join(kept))
PY

# gh-1452: pub.dev server-rejects an upload whose CHANGELOG.md exceeds its
# hard 262144-byte content cap — the guard above already trims to fit, so a
# failure here means even the preamble + the single fresh section is over
# (pathological); a second pass keeping ONLY the fresh section is the last
# resort before the loud fail.
bash "$repo_root/scripts/check_changelog_size.sh" "$changelog" || {
  echo "staged CHANGELOG still over the pub.dev cap — keeping only the fresh section"
  FA_CHANGELOG="$changelog" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

path = os.environ["FA_CHANGELOG"]
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
parts = re.split(r"(?=^## )", text, flags=re.M)
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(parts[0] + parts[1])
PY
  bash "$repo_root/scripts/check_changelog_size.sh" "$changelog"
}
echo "staged CHANGELOG stamped with the v$version section"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring; gh-1522 rework):
#   - scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh — on the STAGED CHANGELOG right after
#     the tag's section is prepended (pre-upload; over-cap trims the oldest
#     staged sections and re-checks);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — on the repo CHANGELOG.md
#     BEFORE staging/upload (the server reject is the worst possible
#     discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

messages.preview: Found the precise regression: on main, the old race hook passed `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` inline; the new tag-race hook dropped that. Let me confirm the new line is an added diff line.

blocks.text:
On main, the gh-1172 race hook raced the **main branch push** with `commit --allow-empty` — and crucially it passed `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` inline. The gh-1522 PR rewrote the hook to race the **tag push** with `tag -a` and DROPPED the inline `-c user.email/-c user.name` flags. The seed commit/tag identity is configured in the seed clone only; the racer clone never gets identity; annotated tags need an identity. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

blocks.text:
Notes on stamp_staged_release.sh:

1. The python trim loop: `if kept and size + b >= cap: break` — the condition `kept` means the first version section is always kept even if it pushes over cap. Since the fresh section was prepended, `versions[0]` is the previous newest section. Keeping it unconditionally could exceed cap; then the fallback below handles it via check_changelog_size.sh. OK.

2. The Unreleased dropping: comment says "drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body" — the python `versions` filter excludes `## Unreleased` sections from being kept, so Unreleased gets dropped from the staged file. But wait — is there logic that ensures the fresh section generated from Unreleased is actually included? Yes: `new = f"## {version}\n{section}\n"` where section comes from release_notes.sh which prefers `## <version>` curated, then `## Unreleased`. OK.

But subtle: if the repo CHANGELOG has a curated `## <version>` section already (same version as being released — shouldn't normally happen), the awk extraction in release_notes.sh: `^## $version$`. Fine.

3. Note in release_notes.sh fallback 1b: the awk prints Unreleased body including leading blank lines? `found { print }` — prints everything after `## Unreleased` until next `##`. Includes blank line right after header. `.strip("\n")` in the python handles edges.

4. check_changelog_size.sh — the header comment now says ci.yml publish job gate checks repo CHANGELOG.md BEFORE staging/upload. But wait — gh-1522's premise: the repo CHANGELOG.md stays bounded by review discipline, and the cap is enforced on the staged file. But if the repo CHANGELOG.md grows past 256 KiB, the publish gate on repo CHANGELOG would fail the release — reintroducing the #1452 class? Let me check ci.yml publish job to see if it still gates on repo CHANGELOG.md size. Let me check.

Also let me review the ci.yml diff fully, and the other workflows (nightly, daily-publish), daily_plan.sh, verify_pubdev_release.sh, install_local.sh, Fastfile, pubspec changes, docs/AGENTS.md.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring; gh-1522 rework):
#   - scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh — on the STAGED CHANGELOG right after
#     the tag's section is prepended (pre-upload; over-cap trims the oldest
#     staged sections and re-checks);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — on the repo CHANGELOG.md
#     BEFORE staging/upload (the server reject is the worst possible
#     discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring; gh-1522 rework):
#   - scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh — on the STAGED CHANGELOG right after
#     the tag's section is prepended (pre-upload; over-cap trims the oldest
#     staged sections and re-checks);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — on the repo CHANGELOG.md
#     BEFORE staging/upload (the server reject is the worst possible
#     discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

blocks.text:
On main, the gh-1172 race hook raced the **main branch push** with `commit --allow-empty` — and crucially it passed `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` inline. The gh-1522 PR rewrote the hook to race the **tag push** with `tag -a` and DROPPED the inline `-c user.email/-c user.name` flags. The seed commit/tag identity is configured in the seed clone only; the racer clone never gets identity; annotated tags need an identity. On hosts with a global git identity (dev machines, and apparently most CI jobs on main... wait, main's hook had inline -c so it never depended on ambient identity).

So this is a regression introduced by this PR: the new hook line `"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main` at new-file line 257 lacks the identity override that the retired line 246 (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit`) had. That's the precise bug: fix = add `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` to the racer's tag command (and it needs an identity only for the tag object).

Also worth noting: tag creation needs GIT_COMMITTER identity; annotated tag requires both author and committer — `-c user.email -c user.name` covers both.

No wait: commit date is when the commit landed; tag cut later. tag_age = now - commit_date > now - tag_date. So the coalesce window (2h) is measured from the last commit on main, not from the last release — the guard could coalesce/skip when the actual tag is older than 2h... no wait, other way: commit_date < tag_date (commit older), so now - commit_date > now - tag_date → measured age LARGER → less coalescing → more frequent releases. Using commit date instead of tag date shrinks effective coalescing when main sat quiet before tagging... hmm, actually no: the tag pins origin/main's tip; the tip's commit date is the most recent merge. If the release job runs right after a push, tag cut ≈ commit date. The 2h window: a NEW push arriving <2h after the last tag's tip commit gets coalesced. That's actually semantically "2h since the last release's content landed," approximately right. Edge: tip commit merged at T, release job delayed (queue), tag cut at T+3h; a push at T+3.5h sees tag_age = 3.5h > 2h → releases again. With tagger date it would be 0.5h → coalesce. Minor behavioral difference in rare cases. SUGGESTION.

Also note: for annotated tags, `git log -1 --format=%ct <tag>` — git log on annotated tag shows the tagged commit (deref). To get the tagger date: `git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag"`. SUGGESTION-level.

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring; gh-1522 rework):
#   - scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh — on the STAGED CHANGELOG right after
#     the tag's section is prepended (pre-upload; over-cap trims the oldest
#     staged sections and re-checks);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — on the repo CHANGELOG.md
#     BEFORE staging/upload (the server reject is the worst possible
#     discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

blocks.text:
On main, the gh-1172 race hook raced the **main branch push** with `commit --allow-empty` — and crucially it passed `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` inline. The gh-1522 PR rewrote the hook to race the **tag push** with `tag -a` and DROPPED the inline `-c user.email/-c user.name` flags. The seed commit/tag identity is configured in the seed clone only; the racer clone never gets identity; annotated tags need an identity. On hosts with a global git identity (dev machines, and apparently most CI jobs on main... wait, main's hook had inline -c so it never depended on ambient identity).

So this is a regression introduced by this PR: the new hook line `"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main` at new-file line 257 lacks the identity override that the retired line 246 (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit`) had. That's the precise bug: fix = add `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` to the racer's tag command (and it needs an identity only for the tag object).

Also worth noting: tag creation needs GIT_COMMITTER identity; annotated tag requires both author and committer — `-c user.email -c user.name` covers both.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring; gh-1522 rework):
#   - scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh — on the STAGED CHANGELOG right after
#     the tag's section is prepended (pre-upload; over-cap trims the oldest
#     staged sections and re-checks);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — on the repo CHANGELOG.md
#     BEFORE staging/upload (the server reject is the worst possible
#     discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

blocks.text:
On main, the gh-1172 race hook raced the **main branch push** with `commit --allow-empty` — and crucially it passed `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` inline. The gh-1522 PR rewrote the hook to race the **tag push** with `tag -a` and DROPPED the inline `-c user.email/-c user.name` flags. The seed commit/tag identity is configured in the seed clone only; the racer clone never gets identity; annotated tags need an identity. On hosts with a global git identity (dev machines, and apparently most CI jobs on main... wait, main's hook had inline -c so it never depended on ambient identity).

So this is a regression introduced by this PR: the new hook line `"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main` at new-file line 257 lacks the identity override that the retired line 246 (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit`) had. That's the precise bug: fix = add `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` to the racer's tag command (and it needs an identity only for the tag object).

Also worth noting: tag creation needs GIT_COMMITTER identity; annotated tag requires both author and committer — `-c user.email -c user.name` covers both.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

blocks.text:
On main, the gh-1172 race hook raced the **main branch push** with `commit --allow-empty` — and crucially it passed `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` inline. The gh-1522 PR rewrote the hook to race the **tag push** with `tag -a` and DROPPED the inline `-c user.email/-c user.name` flags. The seed commit/tag identity is configured in the seed clone only; the racer clone never gets identity; annotated tags need an identity. On hosts with a global git identity (dev machines, and apparently most CI jobs on main... wait, main's hook had inline -c so it never depended on ambient identity).

So this is a regression introduced by this PR: the new hook line `"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main` at new-file line 257 lacks the identity override that the retired line 246 (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit`) had. That's the precise bug: fix = add `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` to the racer's tag command (and it needs an identity only for the tag object).

Also worth noting: tag creation needs GIT_COMMITTER identity; annotated tag requires both author and committer — `-c user.email -c user.name` covers both.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: CI is red — the race hook's annotated tag in the racer clone fails without an ambient git identity**

The `test-core` leg fails (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`) on both new E1 tests, and `hostile-env` fails on the same two:

- `E1 race — a tag that appeared mid-run rejects the push …` — expected `Tag push raced`, got `Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496`
- `E1 exhaustion — a tag race on every attempt exits 1 …` — expected exit 1, got 0

Root cause: the racer clone gets **no git identity**, and the rewritten hook creates an *annotated* tag (`git tag -a`), which requires one. On hosts without a global `user.name`/`user.email` (GitHub runners, the hostile-env leg) the hook's `git tag -a` dies with `fatal: empty ident name … not allowed` → the racer never pre-pushes the tag → the script's own push succeeds → no race, tests fail. The retired main-push hook this replaces carried the identity inline — `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` — and the rewrite dropped it. I reproduced the exact CI failure locally with `HOME=<empty> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.

Fix — restore the inline identity on the racer's tag command (the seed clone's `git config` does not leak into the racer):

```bash
"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t \
  -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main
```

(Setting `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` in `baseEnv` would work too, but the inline `-c` matches the fixture's established pattern.)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the repo-file changelog gate still blocks releases — this claim (and the ticket's core promise) is not delivered**

This sentence says the in-repo CHANGELOG's size "can never block a release again" — but the `publish` job still runs `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` on the **repo file** as a hard pre-staging gate (ci.yml, "Publish gate" step): an over-cap repo CHANGELOG fails the whole publish job, exactly the #1452 class gh-1522 was opened to retire. The ticket is explicit: *"even if it inflates, the published artifact's changelog is generated — the 256 KiB cap can no longer block a release."*

The staged-side protection is already complete without the repo-file gate: `stamp_staged_release.sh` trims the oldest staged sections to fit, re-measures with `check_changelog_size.sh`, and has a last-resort single-section fallback before failing loud — the uploaded artifact can never trip the server cap. (Note the repo file isn't even what pub packs; the staged tree is.)

Options:
- Make the repo-file check **non-blocking** in the publish job (a `::warning::` pointing at `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`), keeping the staged check as the real gate; or
- Move the repo-file check to a non-release surface (Static gates / nightly) so the release train can't die on it.

Either way, this header (and `docs/ci.md`'s matching claim) should reflect reality. `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` currently pins the release-blocking wiring (`the guard belongs in the gate step, ahead of staging`) — update it with whichever direction is chosen.

blocks.text:
On main, the gh-1172 race hook raced the **main branch push** with `commit --allow-empty` — and crucially it passed `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` inline. The gh-1522 PR rewrote the hook to race the **tag push** with `tag -a` and DROPPED the inline `-c user.email/-c user.name` flags. The seed commit/tag identity is configured in the seed clone only; the racer clone never gets identity; annotated tags need an identity. On hosts with a global git identity (dev machines, and apparently most CI jobs on main... wait, main's hook had inline -c so it never depended on ambient identity).

So this is a regression introduced by this PR: the new hook line `"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main` at new-file line 257 lacks the identity override that the retired line 246 (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit`) had. That's the precise bug: fix = add `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` to the racer's tag command (and it needs an identity only for the tag object).

Also worth noting: tag creation needs GIT_COMMITTER identity; annotated tag requires both author and committer — `-c user.email -c user.name` covers both.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: CI is red — the race hook's annotated tag in the racer clone fails without an ambient git identity**

The `test-core` leg fails (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`) on both new E1 tests, and `hostile-env` fails on the same two:

- `E1 race — a tag that appeared mid-run rejects the push …` — expected `Tag push raced`, got `Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496`
- `E1 exhaustion — a tag race on every attempt exits 1 …` — expected exit 1, got 0

Root cause: the racer clone gets **no git identity**, and the rewritten hook creates an *annotated* tag (`git tag -a`), which requires one. On hosts without a global `user.name`/`user.email` (GitHub runners, the hostile-env leg) the hook's `git tag -a` dies with `fatal: empty ident name … not allowed` → the racer never pre-pushes the tag → the script's own push succeeds → no race, tests fail. The retired main-push hook this replaces carried the identity inline — `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` — and the rewrite dropped it. I reproduced the exact CI failure locally with `HOME=<empty> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.

Fix — restore the inline identity on the racer's tag command (the seed clone's `git config` does not leak into the racer):

```bash
"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t \
  -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main
```

(Setting `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` in `baseEnv` would work too, but the inline `-c` matches the fixture's established pattern.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: no behavioral test executes `stamp_staged_release.sh` — the ticket's riskiest new script is pinned by string assertions only**

The stamper is the linchpin of gh-1522 (a bad stamp ships `0.0.0-dev` or a malformed changelog to pub.dev), and its riskiest logic — the Python section split, the `## Unreleased` fold, the cap-trim loop, the last-resort single-section fallback — is only `contains`/`indexOf`-pinned here and in `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart`. The nightly dry-run would catch a crash, but nothing asserts the staged *content*: e.g. that the generated section actually lands under `## <version>`, that the staged file no longer shows an `## Unreleased` header, that the version stamp is exactly the tag, and that an over-cap staged file trims oldest-first keeping the fresh section.

This file already has the fixture harness for it (temp dir + `Process.runSync('bash', [stamp_staged_release.sh, …])`, same as `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` exercises `check_changelog_size.sh` behaviorally). A small behavioral group — stamp a fixture stage, assert pubspec + changelog bytes, over-cap trim, missing-version-line loud fail — would close the gap. (Also worth one case: a repo CHANGELOG that already carries a curated `## <version>` section for the same version — today the staged file would show that section twice, since the stamper prepends the generated one and keeps the existing one.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: generated changelog section is missing blank lines — raw output runs sections together**

`new = f"## {version}\n{section}\n"` produces (verified against a fixture run):

```markdown
## 1.0.550
- something pending
## 1.0.549

- old entry
```

No blank line after the section header, and none between the fresh section and the next `## ` — the published pub.dev changelog renders it acceptably, but the raw markdown is scruffy and inconsistent with the hand-curated sections. Consider `new = f"\n## {version}\n\n{section}\n\n"` (or `.strip()` the section and re-join with explicit blank lines) so the stamped file matches the repo's existing formatting convention.

💡 **SUGGESTION: coalesce age reads the tagged commit's date, not the tag's tagger date**

`git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag"` dereferences the annotated tag to the commit, so `tag_age` measures the committer date of origin/main's tip *at tag time* — not when the tag was cut. The two diverge whenever commits sat pending on main before the cron/dispatch cut the tag (the common catch-up path this file exists for): a tag cut 10 minutes ago can read hours old, so a new push would not be coalesced even though the 2h window since the *release* hasn't elapsed — the extra releases are exactly what this guard (and the pub.dev ~12/day rate limit) exists to prevent. Use the tag object date instead:

```bash
tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag") ))
```

💡 **SUGGESTION: step name no longer describes what it verifies**

`Verify tag matches pubspec version` now does the inverse of its name — it checks that the committed pubspec is still the `0.0.0-dev` placeholder and no longer compares the tag to the pubspec at all (the binaries-job twin was already renamed to `Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder`). The stale name will mislead the next person reading a failed run. Rename to match the twin.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"
